task: agent-workroom: WebXR headset room, voice first, with controller pointing
errors: Local run_workflow_locally: agent-permission-harness-ci's byte-identical-report test failed because the repository file count changed between its two runs (11777 vs 11778) while other local checks were writing files; not caused by this diff.

doc_friction.issue: The 'Ideas' list said a WebXR mode 'would need WebGL'; true, but nothing said Quest Browser lacks SpeechRecognition, which decides whether a voice-first headset app needs an on-device model. Now recorded in the README.

deviations.why: `promptctl.py route` drew the research track at random; the owner's message asked directly for venture work, so the run followed ventures/1 instead.
deviations.result: Feature shipped on the venture the request fits.

goal: A headset (Meta Quest) app to manage the coding agents working on this repo, driven mainly by voice, with normal VR controls.
notes: Built on the existing agent-workroom venture (owner 2026-10-24 'vr like workplace for working with agents'). Verification: node --test on engine/page/xr/vr tests, 49 pass; run_venture_tests.py agent-workroom ok. Headless Chromium (SwiftShader) at 1280x900 and 390x800 with a mocked GitHub API: 3 PRs -> tasks on Claude/Codex/Dependabot desks, check runs mark #2 failing, 'go to Codex's desk' moves the camera, 'ask claude on 4' refused (local task), 'ask claude on 2 ...' + 'confirm' POSTs '@claude look at the failing test\n\n_Sent from Agent Workroom._' with the bearer token; 2D page sees the same 4 tasks; no page errors; no horizontal scroll. Fake WebXR device (stubbed navigator.xr/session/frames/controller): headset frame loop ran 31-42 frames, no errors; right stick snap-turned 30 degrees. On-device speech through the real jsDelivr CDN and Hugging Face model: Whisper tiny.en q8/wasm transcribed the 11 s JFK sample word for word in 8.6 s. Push to talk end to end (Chromium fake mic playing the clip -> voice.mjs -> Whisper -> run()): 'Added task 1: And so my fellow America!' (clip cut at 5 s). Not verified on a real headset: rendering, controller mapping and speech latency on Quest are untested; Quest Browser's lack of SpeechRecognition is from Meta forum threads, not checked on a device.
